definition.alternative: Preference divergence decays to zero across all tested configurations when noise is controlled.
assumptions: Memory-augmented architectures retain internal state representing historical trajectory.
Episodic retrieval influences subsequent action probabilities.
Deterministic gridworld environments isolate path-dependence from stochastic noise.
definition.falsification: Measured divergence slope is reliably negative, indicating convergence rather than persistent path-dependent preference formation.
definition.statement: Memory-augmented agents exhibit persistent non-zero policy divergence over extended training horizons in deterministic gridworld environments when historical state trajectories are weighted by episodic retrieval, subject to bounded stochastic noise constraints.
definition.uncertainty: It remains to be established whether the observed variance reflects true path-dependent preference splitting or measurement artifact under tighter controls.

definition.method: Execute a controlled gridworld simulation measuring policy divergence over 60000 steps with tightened variance controls.
definition.stop: Stop if measurement variance invalidates slope estimation.
definition.success: Divergence slope remains non-negative with reduced variance.

proposal.summary: This cycle advances the investigation into path-dependent preference formation under memory-augmented architectures by formulating a refined experimental iteration and hypothesis revision.
